{{c|{{sc|Ode 4, Stanzas 1 and 2. The {{tooltip|Yî Pho|Yù Pú}}.}}}}
{{dhr|0%}}
{{smaller block/s}}
{{c|{{asc|In praise of [[w:King Wen of Zhou|king Wăn]], celebrating his influence, dignity in the temple services, activity, and capacity to rule.}}}}
{{smaller block/e}}

{{center block/s}}
Abundant is the growth of the buckthorn and shrubby trees,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Supplying firewood; yea, stores of it<ref>It is difficult to trace the connexion between-these allusive lines and the rest of the piece.</ref>.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Elegant and dignified was our prince and king;{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
On the left and the right they hastened to him.

Elegant and dignified was our prince and king;{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
On his left and his right they bore their half-mace (libation-cups)<ref>Here we have the lord of [[w:Predynastic Zhou|''K''âu]] in his [[w:Ancestral temple|ancestral temple]], assisted by his ministers or great officers in pouring out the libations to the spirits of the departed. {{anchor+|libation_cup|The libation-cup}} was fitted with a handle of jade, that used by the king having a complete [[wikt:圭|{{sp|kwe|i}}]], the obelisk-like symbol of rank, while the cups used by a minister had for a handle only half a {{sp|kwe|i}}.</ref>:—{{lb}}They
bore them with solemn gravity,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
As beseemed such eminent officers.
{{center block/e}}
<section end="ode4" />
<section begin="ode5" />{{dhr}}
{{c|{{sc|Ode 5. The {{tooltip|Han Lû|Hàn Lù}}.}}}}
{{dhr|0%}}
{{smaller block/s}}
{{hanging indent/s}}
{{asc|In praise of the virtue of [[w:King Wen of Zhou|king Wăn]], blessed by his ancestors, and raised to the highest dignity without seeking of his own.}}
{{hanging indent/e}}
{{smaller block/e}}

{{center block/s}}
Look at the foot of the {{tooltip|Han|Hàn}}<ref>Where mount [[wikt:旱|Han]] was cannot now be determined.</ref>,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
How abundantly grow the hazel and arrow-thorn<ref>As the foot of the hill was favourable to vegetable growth, so were [[w:King Wen of Zhou|king Wăn]]'s natural qualities to his distinction and advancement.</ref>.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Easy and self-possessed was our prince,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
In his pursuit of dignity (still) easy and self-possessed.

Massive is that libation-cup of jade,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
With the
